decision: The whole system design story is two problems, each solved end to end
why: A founder remembers two stories; a catalog of architectures blurs into boxes.
value: Engineering and product judgment, each shown on a problem the audience recognizes.

decision: Plain language on the surface, engineering one key away (E), presentation one key away (F)
why: If a non-technical person understands it, a technical person will too, and the engineer still gets the detail.
alternative: Separate pages for technical and non-technical readers.
value: One page serves both, without switching tabs in a call.

decision: The story pages are static Astro served under /system-design by the shell
why: They need no server and must stay under 60 kB of JS per route; the Astro zone already exists.
value: Fast, free pages with no new deploy target.

decision: The earlier architecture pages stay as engineering deep dives below the story
why: Engineers can still follow every hop; founders never have to.
value: Fewer, better entry points, with depth kept.

decision: The 80/20 banner closes the intro: build what makes you different, buy what everyone needs
why: Every choice on the following pages is an instance of that one rule, including keeping this portfolio free.
value: The audience leaves with the rule, not the components.
